### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS), daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS), daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS), daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/schema.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS), daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/ui/reports.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `current_user (literal, 44 pages)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa1134c61ec0f6538b25eda31dcd4b6e1ebbb7fd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `73139584aeb839054b8cebbc94322086214f4578` — the merge of head `1215cab9c7c93bb636461a9ea5ee1027034b8830` into base `fa1134c61ec0f6538b25eda31dcd4b6e1ebbb7fd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 73139584aeb839054b8cebbc94322086214f4578 && git checkout 73139584aeb839054b8cebbc94322086214f4578
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fa1134c61ec0f6538b25eda31dcd4b6e1ebbb7fd 1215cab9c7c93bb636461a9ea5ee1027034b8830 && git checkout -B drift-repro fa1134c61ec0f6538b25eda31dcd4b6e1ebbb7fd && git merge --no-ff 1215cab9c7c93bb636461a9ea5ee1027034b8830

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa1134c61ec0f6538b25eda31dcd4b6e1ebbb7fd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fa1134c61ec0f6538b25eda31dcd4b6e1ebbb7fd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fbd58d8ee0e0f6ecb3e69d8fa876068010eb7319`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/stored-expression-inputs.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/stored-expression-inputs.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.object-formula-writes.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.stored-expression-cross-record-input-refused.ts + .changeset/32529-stored-expression-inputs.md (levels and the `registered` marker only)

Read, not reviewed: `packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts` (`planStoredExpressions`, `formulaPlanEntry`, `applyFormulaPlan`, `computeStoredExpressions`), `engine-insert.ts`, `engine-security-resolvers.ts` (`resolveFormulaRelated`), `validation/rule-validator.ts` (`collectReferenceTraversals`), `packages/formula/src/relationship-traversal.ts`, `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts` (`registerBoundStdLib`, `buildScope`), `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts` (`referenceTargetOf`), `packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts`, all at the head. Card #32529 and #32554 with every comment; ruling 6816315099.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, narrowed (right in direction, incomplete in extent).** A non-`formula` field with an `expression` that reads through an AUTHORED `lookup` / `master_detail` / `user` / `tree` field of the same object is now an `error` at `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` and at the object door. Refuse is inside the ruling ("refuse or warn at authoring"). The extent is narrower than the PR, the changeset, `os explain` and the ADR-0087 entry say: see must-fix 1.
- **"Stored expression" test: right.** `storedExpressionInputIssues` returns for `def.type === 'formula' || !def.expression`; `planStoredExpressions` plans `def.type !== 'formula' && def.expression`. Same predicate. A non-CEL dialect answers nothing on both sides (`celSourceOf` / `celSourceOfSlot`).
- **The engine does resolve the hop at write: right.** `engine-insert.ts` hands `computeStoredExpressions` a `relatedFor` that is `resolveFormulaRelated`, which loads one hop per reference field under the caller's authority; `formulaPlanEntry` plans the hop with `collectReferenceTraversals` over the registered schema's fields. Nothing recomputes on a change to the related row. The premise of the refusal holds.
- **No false positive on a same-row read: right.** `analyzeRelationshipTraversals` reports a traversal only for `record.F.LEAF` in the four member spellings; a method receiver (`record.name.startsWith(…)`), a comprehension receiver and a non-literal index are bare reads. A traversed field that is not a reference (`referenceTargetOf` answers undefined: json, object, composite) is skipped. `id` alone is admitted, matching `undeclaredRelatedFields`' treatment of the primary key (#8215).
- **Volatile list: right, read off the tree.** `registerBoundStdLib` registers exactly four functions over the bound clock (`now`, `today`, `daysFromNow`, `daysAgo`); `buildScope` mounts the one `EvalUser` under `current_user`, `user`, `ctx.user`, `os.user`; `can` and `hasCapability` are the two receiver methods the permission binding answers. `applyFormulaPlan` passes `now, timezone, user, org, permissions, optionLabels, record` and no `env`, so nothing else is bound. `os.org` is `execCtx.tenantId`, and `label()` on a stored expression reads `declaredOptionLabels` (not the reader's locale): both exclusions have a real reason.
- **Public surface, additive: right.** `ExprIssue.rule` (optional), two exported ids, two `os explain` entries. `rule: i.rule ?? EXPRESSION_INVALID` leaves every other finding of the pass as it was.
- **Doors: right.** The entry's `runtimeTypes` already includes `object`, the member runs inside `judgeFieldFormula`, which the object write runs; severity maps unchanged, so the error is a 422 and the warning an advisory. The five door cases in `runtime-gate.object-formula-writes.test.ts` pin refusal, re-save, advisory, controls and parity.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are right for an accept-set narrowing with a semantic entry. `@objectstack/lint` minor and `@objectstack/spec` minor match the 18.x precedent for a BREAKING narrowing with a registered entry (`.changeset/29904-…`, `29926-…`: lint minor + spec minor, `registered ID`). The marker names the id the entry file declares. `Check Changeset` and the three `Lint ·` gate families are `success` on this head. The test, build and type-check runs (31) were still `in_progress` when this record was written: no gate verdict is read from them here.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: empty. Dev `deviations` (widened file surface, four commits, a stray pid file): the lane seat's to accept, none touches the contract.
- **Unanswered on the card, escalated (must-fix 2).** Triage's correction 6819979060 on #32529 (09:32Z, an hour before the dev report) says first-party exposure is 1, not 0: HotCRM `src/sales/objects/forecast.object.ts:152` `display_title`, a stored field reading `record.?owner_id.?name`, stored on purpose by #24981 A. The dev report says `premise_still_valid: true`, exposure 0, and does not mention it; the PR body's 维护者速读 says 第一方存量实测为 0. The ruling's condition is "count existing exposure first".
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed`: the three skill files named do teach a stored field carrying a formula's `expression` with no word on its inputs (`relationships.md:330`, `field-types.md:131`, `dashboards.md:100`), so the line is honest about them. It is incomplete: see should-fix 1.

### ④ Design judgment

**must-fix 1 — a hop through a registry-injected reference column is not judged, and the engine resolves it.** `validate-expressions.ts` builds `fieldDefs` from `fieldList`, the object's AUTHORED `fields`. `owner_id`, `created_by` and `updated_by` are injected at registration as `{ type: 'lookup', reference: 'sys_user' }` (`OWNER_FIELD_DEF`, `AUDIT_FIELD_DEFS`), and the engine plans a stored expression from `this._registry.getObject(object)`, whose fields carry them. So on an object that does not declare `owner_id`, `display: { type: 'text', expression: 'record.owner_id.name' }` gets `referenceTargetOf(undefined)`, is skipped, and passes clean, while the write reads the user's name and stores it, stale on the next rename. This is the most common cross-record read there is, and it is the shape of the one first-party row the card thread names. A field an `objectExtensions` entry adds is missed the same way (the pass reads the authored body; `objectsAsServed` and `injectedColumnDefsFor` are already imported in this file). Three published sentences are false on the tree as a result: the entry's `surface` ("through a lookup, master_detail, user or tree field of the same object … by any spelling the engine resolves"), the same sentence in `os explain`, and the entry's `acceptanceCriteria` (a clean `objectstack validate` does not show the stack is free of the read). No test covers an injected column. Fix: judge the hop through the definitions the registry serves (authored first, then `injectedColumnDefsFor(obj)`, and the folded extension fields), with a pin for `record.owner_id.name` and for `record.created_by.name`, and an `ownership: 'none'` control.

**must-fix 2 — the exposure count the ruling asks for is not the one on the PR.** The in-repo count is sound: 3 stored expression fields in `examples/**` (`quantity * unit_price` twice, one currency rounding), none with a hop or a volatile input; every `today()` there is on a `Field.formula`. But the card's own thread records a first-party hit outside this repo, and neither the report nor the PR body answers it. Both branches are a problem: if HotCRM declares `owner_id`, this rule refuses its build and its next save and the migration is not settled; if it does not, the rule is silent on it (must-fix 1) and becomes a refusal the moment that is fixed. The PR body's "0" and the report's premise line must be corrected to name the row, and the seat or the maintainer must record how HotCRM's `display_title` is migrated before this lands.

**should-fix 1 — `Skills-docs:` omits the hand-written docs that teach the same thing.** `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx:106` tells an author to move a composite title to "a stored computed field (a non-formula field with an `expression`, written on write) when import, sort or search must match it", directly above a title that reads `record.customer.name`: followed literally, it now leads into the refusal. `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx:703` and `validation-rules.mdx:371` describe `expression` on a stored field with no word on either input. The follow-up line should name them.

**nit 1 — the user namespace is matched in two of the four member spellings.** `volatileReads` counts `os.user` and `os.?user`, not `os['user']` or `ctx['user']`, while the hop half counts the index spellings through `readRootMembers`. A warning only, so no contract effect.

**nit 2 — the remedy names a `summary` on the related object whatever the reference is.** For the measured case it is right (a `summary` of `days` on the employee, a `formula` there times `daily_hours`), and it does not claim to carry the parent's value down, which was triage's objection. For a `user` hop the message reads "compute it on 'sys_user': a `summary` field there", a platform object, and `recomputeSummaries` infers the child link only from a `lookup` / `master_detail`. The formula and flow repairs stand in every case.

**Holds.** The `id` exclusion; the comprehension shadowing; the `formula` control; the entry's sentences on the parse ("an object row stored before this release stays stored, loads and keeps computing"), which is true since nothing in the schema or the engine changes; the door list and `OS_ALLOW_UNLINTED_METADATA_WRITES=1` (`runtime-authoring-gate.ts`); the warning having no entry.

Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcSbLCxEmyHf9upz3pz`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
